http://www.amazon.com/Victorinox-One-Hand-Trekker-German-Multi-Tool/dp/B001B197RE/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1440248578&sr=8-1&keywords=victorinox+german+army+knife

They also make the Sentinel, with just one blade:

http://www.amazon.com/Victorinox-Swiss-Sentinel-Pocket-Knife/dp/B001QUXH5S/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1440248839&sr=8-1&keywords=victorinox+sentinel+serrated

The best solution is two blades, one fully serrated, one fully straight. I used to have a nice folding buck knife in this configuration that was my EDC for many years, but it is discontinued now.

There is nothing serrations can do that a good sharp plain edge can't. People always say working on the docks/sailing/boating you need a serrated knife. My maintained edc's go through rope like butter, a serrated knife takes more sawing, and work. In my experience at least. Just keep your knives sharp and ditch the serrations!
